aliases: US-SW-TULAROSA (adjacent Tularosa Basin below the pass)

city_center.name: Cloudcroft village (Burro Avenue) + Alamogordo below
city_center.landmark: Sacramento Mountains alpine village at ~8,600-9,000 ft, surrounded by the Lincoln National Forest; a 4,400-ft drop west to White Sands and Alamogordo on the Tularosa Basin floor
city_center.notes: Cloudcroft is one of the highest communities in the Southwest, an alpine pine village founded as a logging and vacation town on the El Paso & Northeastern Railroad; the everyday grocery run drops to Alamogordo below. sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudcroft,_New_Mexico; newmexicomagazine.org Cloudcroft; discovercloudcroft.com.

featured_frontier.hook: A hot stack on the porch of a pine-timber lodge at 9,000 ft, Lincoln National Forest in the frost while White Sands shimmers 4,400 ft below -- 'the land above the clouds' breakfast
featured_frontier.photo_cue: cast-iron stack on a pine-timber porch, frosted ponderosa, White Sands glinting far below at dawn
featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: high-mountain cool-climate apples + honey; alpine pine-village dawn

audience: Alpine mountain-village families + Alamogordo basin households; Walmart Alamogordo + Albertsons shoppers, cool-forest getaway above the desert

cultural_notes: Cloudcroft sits at nearly 8,700 ft in the Sacramento Mountains -- one of the highest communities in the US, 'the land above the clouds' -- a pine-forest alpine island above the surrounding desert (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudcroft,_New_Mexico; newmexicomagazine.org; localobserverdaily.com)

the village was established in the late 1890s as a logging and vacation town by developers of the El Paso & Northeastern Railroad, which pushed a line up the summit to harvest the forests (source: en.wikipedia.org Cloudcroft; newmexicomagazine.org)
Cloudcroft opens onto 1.1 million acres of Lincoln National Forest and some of the darkest night skies in New Mexico; a 4,400-ft drop leads to White Sands (source: discovercloudcroft.com)
the everyday retail base is down in Alamogordo on the Tularosa Basin floor; the village itself is a small frontier grocery gap (INFERRED retail framing from geography -- verify)

design_palette._provenance_note: pine timber + board-and-batten + trestle grounded in Cloudcroft's logging/railroad heritage and alpine forest setting (en.wikipedia.org Cloudcroft; newmexicomagazine.org).
